title: Second-Largest Distinct Number
problem_statement: Read a list of integers and print its second-largest distinct value. Distinct means duplicate occurrences count as the same value: for example, the second-largest distinct value in [8, 8, 5] is 5. If fewer than two distinct values are present, print `NONE`. Use one pass with a constant number of tracking variables instead of sorting the list.
input_format: The first line contains an integer n, the number of values. The second line contains exactly n space-separated integers.
output_format: Print the second-largest distinct integer value. If the list contains fewer than two distinct values, print exactly `NONE`.
starter_code:
def main():
    n = int(input())
    numbers = list(map(int, input().split()))

    # TODO: Track the largest and second-largest distinct values while scanning.
    # TODO: Do not treat another copy of the largest value as a distinct runner-up.

    print("NONE")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

public_samples.explanation: The largest distinct value is 7 and the next distinct value is 5.
The duplicate 9s count as one distinct value; 8 is the next-largest distinct value.
-2 is largest and -5 is the second-largest distinct value.
There is only one distinct value, so no second-largest distinct value exists.
A one-element list cannot contain a second distinct value.

hints: The second-largest value must be different from the largest value; repeated copies do not create another rank.
As you scan, keep track of the best two distinct values seen so far. Think through what should happen when a new value is bigger than the current largest.
For each number, update the largest and second-largest trackers in order. Ignore a value equal to the largest, and only print the second tracker if it was set.
common_beginner_mistakes: Sorting the whole list despite the intended one-pass comparison approach.
Treating the second copy of the largest number as the second-largest distinct value.
Initializing both trackers to 0, which fails when all values are negative.
Updating the largest without first moving the old largest into the second-largest position.
Using only `n > 1` to decide whether a second distinct value exists; duplicates may leave only one distinct value.
Printing a default numeric value when no second distinct value exists instead of printing `NONE`.
completion_criteria: Reads n and exactly n integers in the specified two-line format.
Finds the second-largest distinct value in a single pass without sorting.
Handles duplicates, negative values, and any input order.
Prints exactly `NONE` when fewer than two distinct values exist.
Prints only the answer value or `NONE`, with no extra text.
Passes all public samples and separately maintained private tests.
